column1: The first thing that strikes you is that the car belongs to Marie. Then you see the paramedics working over a body. Panic begins to overwhelm you as you race to the ambulance.
column2: 你第一眼注意到的是，那輛車是 Marie 的。接著你看見救護人員正在搶救一具身體。你在奔向救護車的同時，恐慌開始淹沒了你。

column1: You jump in the ambulance and respond code three to the hospital.
column2: 你跳上救護車，鳴笛全速趕往醫院。

column1: Marie is rushed to Lytton General Emergency where doctors begin the race to save her life.
column2: Marie 被緊急送往 Lytton 綜合醫院急診室，醫生們立刻展開搶救。

column1: They work through the night, fighting to stabilize Marie's condition. Sonny spends hours of agony in the waiting room. Although they manage to save her life, Marie remains in a coma.
column2: 他們徹夜搶救，設法穩住 Marie 的狀況。Sonny 在候診室裡煎熬了好幾個鐘頭。雖然保住了她的性命，Marie 卻陷入昏迷。

column1: When he's finally allowed to see her, Sonny holds her hand until the pre-dawn hours, hoping and searching for some sign that she'll come back to him.
column2: 終於獲准進去探視後，Sonny 一直握著她的手直到破曉前，盼望能看見她甦醒的徵兆。

column1: Physically and emotionally exhausted, you decide to go home and get some rest.
column2: 身心俱疲的你，決定回家休息一下。

column1: Looks like another one bit the dust, eh?
column2: 看來又掛了一個，是吧？

column1: I understand you were here before they removed the victim. Did you catch any dying words? Notice any signs of sexual assault? Anything at all?
column2: 我聽說被害人被抬走之前你就在場。她有沒有留下遺言？有沒有性侵的跡象？隨便什麼線索都好？

column1: Responding to your silence, the reporter says...
column2: 面對你的沉默，這名記者接著說……

column1: Well, if YOU don't want to talk to me, I'll just get the information elsewhere!
column2: 好啊，你不肯跟我說，那我自己去別的地方打聽！

column1: Listen, you little blood sucking piece of FILTH! The victim was my wife! You guys are all the same. Now get outta here before I forget that I'm wearing this badge!
column2: 聽好了，你這個吸血的人渣！被害人是我老婆！你們這種人都一個樣。趁我還記得自己戴著這面警徽，滾出去！

column1: I'll give your paper some details alright!... All about how I rearranged your face!
column2: 我這就給你的報社一些細節……講講我是怎麼把你的臉重新排列的！

column1: Oh, Geez! Look Officer I- I'm terribly sorry!
column2: 天啊！聽著，警官，我……我真的很抱歉！

column1: I'm just trying to get the facts. I thought you cops liked that kind of loose talk - helps keep things from getting too serious, know what I mean?
column2: 我只是想弄清楚事實。我還以為你們警察喜歡那種嘴上開開玩笑，讓場面不要太沉重，你懂我的意思吧？

column1: Here's my card. If there is anything I can ever help you with, Officer, give me a ring, huh? Again, sorry about your wife.
column2: 這是我的名片。以後有什麼需要幫忙的，警官，打給我，好嗎？還有，你太太的事，我很遺憾。

column1: You feel a moment of remorse for your outburst, and almost say 'thanks', but fortunately the moment passes.
column2: 你為自己剛才的失控感到一絲愧疚，差點就脫口說出「謝謝」，幸好那股衝動很快就過去了。

column1: The officer is intent on his search and ignores you.
column2: 那名警員專注在搜查上，沒理會你。

column1: Your batteries appear to be dead.
column2: 你的電池似乎沒電了。

column1: You catch the glint of an object lying just beneath Marie's car.
column2: 你瞥見 Marie 的車底下有個東西閃著光。

column1: You pick up what appears to be a medallion. Upon closer inspection you recognize it to be a "Bronze Star" war medal.
column2: 你撿起一個看似勳章的東西。仔細一看，你認出那是一枚「銅星勳章」。

column1: It's a very LARGE streetlamp.
column2: 這是一盞非常大的路燈。

column1: You try to search the area, but it's just too dark to see anything. Perhaps you should come back when it's light.
column2: 你試著搜查這一帶，但天色太暗什麼也看不清。或許等天亮再回來比較好。

column1: The parking lot blacktop.
column2: 停車場的柏油地面。

column1: Some of the mall's stores are undergoing renovation.
column2: 這座購物中心有幾家店正在整修。

column1: That store is closed.
column2: 那家店已經打烊了。

column1: Sidewalks connect the store fronts.
column2: 人行道連接著各家店面。

column1: The flashlight is already on.
column2: 手電筒已經是開著的。

column1: That's the Army Recruiter's office.
column2: 那是陸軍徵兵處。

column1: The Army Recruiter's office is closed for the night.
column2: 陸軍徵兵處今晚已經打烊了。

column1: That's the shop of "Zak" the keymaker.
column2: 那是鎖匠「Zak」的店。

column1: Zak's key shop is closed for the night.
column2: Zak 的鑰匙店今晚已經打烊了。

column1: Marie's Trans Am still sits in the poorly lit parking lot of the mall. You scan the car for clues... but find nothing.
column2: Marie 的 Trans Am 仍停在購物中心那燈光昏暗的停車場裡。你仔細檢查車子想找線索……但一無所獲。

column1: What can I do for you?
column2: 有什麼我能幫你的？

column1: Need a key made?
column2: 要配鑰匙嗎？

column1: I make keys for big locks, small locks, clocks, cars, tanks and banks. What do you need fella?
column2: 大鎖小鎖、時鐘、汽車、坦克、銀行的鑰匙我都配。老兄，你要什麼？

column1: What, you want another one? You got a family of ten moving in or what?
column2: 怎麼，你還要一把？你家是搬來十口人喔？

column1: Ah yes! No problem with this little jewel. I'll have a copy in a second.
column2: 啊，好！這個小寶貝沒問題。馬上就給你配好。

column1: Sorry, but this key says "Do Not Duplicate."
column2: 抱歉，這把鑰匙上寫著「禁止複製」。

column1: Here you are fella, that'll be two fifty.
column2: 拿去吧老兄，兩塊五。

column1: You give Zak his two dollars and fifty cents.
column2: 你付給 Zak 兩塊五毛錢。

column1: Thanks buddy... Another day another two dollars and fifty cents.
column2: 謝啦老兄……又是平凡的一天，又賺了兩塊五。

column1: You what? No money? Do I look like an idiot to you? Get outta my shop!
column2: 你說什麼？沒錢？你當我是白痴嗎？滾出我的店！

column1: Sorry, this key says 'Do Not Duplicate' on it.
column2: 抱歉，這把鑰匙上寫著「禁止複製」。

column1: What do you want me to do with that?  I'm a KEY maker, for crying out loud.
column2: 你要我拿這個怎麼辦？我是配鑰匙的，老天爺啊。

column1: Just giving away money, Sonny?
column2: 錢多到花不完喔，Sonny？

column1: You don't have the correct change.
column2: 你身上沒有剛好的零錢。

column1: Morales is making a phone call.
column2: Morales 正在講電話。

column1: That's Officer Pat Morales, your partner.
column2: 那是 Pat Morales 警員，你的搭檔。

column1: You retrieve the bronze star.
column2: 你取回了那枚銅星勳章。

column1: OH NO! you think... "This just can't be!!  Not Marie!"
column2: 「不！」你心想……「這不可能！不會是 Marie！」

column1: What's wrong with her!
column2: 她怎麼了！

column1: Multiple stab wounds.  Damage unclear.
column2: 多處刺傷，傷勢尚不明。

column1: It doesn't look good.  We have to get her to the hospital STAT.
column2: 情況不樂觀，我們得立刻送她去醫院！

column1: We're ready.  If you're goin', you'd better climb in, Officer.
column2: 我們準備好了。你要一起去的話，最好趕快上車，警官。

column1: You see something clutched in Marie's hand.
column2: 你看見 Marie 手裡緊握著什麼東西。

column1: It's empty.
column2: 裡面是空的。

column1: You remove what appears to be a chain from Marie's hand.
column2: 你從 Marie 手中取出一條鍊子。

column1: Looking at the broken chain you think... "Marie must have pulled this from the attacker's neck!"
column2: 看著這條斷掉的鍊子，你心想……「Marie 一定是從攻擊者脖子上扯下這個的！」

column1: And you ponder the thought... "I just wonder if something else was on this chain."
column2: 你不禁思忖……「不知道這條鍊子上原本是不是還掛著別的東西。」

column1: Her hand feels cold.
column2: 她的手感覺冰冷。

column1: You try waking her, but she doesn't respond.
column2: 你試著叫醒她，但她毫無反應。

column1: You drop your partner off at the station then drive yourself home for some needed rest.
column2: 你把搭檔送回警局後，自己開車回家好好休息。

column1: Feeling physically and emotionally drained, you drive home.
column2: 感到身心俱疲的你，開車回家。

column1: Officer Bonds, I'm Dr. Wagner, the resident neurosurgeon.
column2: Bonds 警官，我是 Wagner 醫師，這裡的住院神經外科醫師。

column1: I'm sorry to say that your wife's condition is still quite serious.  She's suffering from internal injuries sustained from the multiple stab wounds.
column2: 很遺憾，你太太的狀況仍然相當嚴重。她因為多處刺傷而有內臟損傷。

column1: How long she will remain in a coma is anyone's guess.
column2: 她會昏迷多久，誰也說不準。

column1: In my experience, the presence of a loved one urging the patient back from that void is an incalculable asset.
column2: 依我的經驗，親人在旁呼喚，勸病人從那片虛無中回來，是一種難以估量的幫助。

column1: We're doing all we can for her physically, but you might be the only one who can reach her now.
column2: 我們在醫療上已經盡了全力，但現在或許只有你才能喚得回她。

column1: The nurse found this chain clutched in your wife's hand.
column2: 護理師在你太太手中發現了這條鍊子。

column1: Sergeant Bonds, you look beat.  You really should go home and try to get some rest.  There's nothing to be done for your wife right now.
column2: Bonds 警佐，你看起來累壞了。你真的該回家休息一下。現在你太太這邊也沒什麼你能做的了。

column1: We can all feel good about the fact that Marie is alive.
column2: Marie 還活著，這一點就值得我們慶幸了。

column1: Marie!  Please come back, Baby.  I can't go on without you.
column2: Marie！求求妳醒過來，寶貝。沒有妳我活不下去。

column1: You fight to pull yourself together.
column2: 你強忍情緒，努力讓自己振作起來。

column1: I...I've gotta go now, Babe.  You need your rest.  It's been a rough night.
column2: 我……我得先走了，寶貝。妳需要休息。今晚真的很難熬。

column1: I'll get the bastard who did this, Babe.  I SWEAR IT!
column2: 我會抓到做這件事的混蛋，寶貝。我發誓！

column1: As a fellow officer drives you back to your car at the mall, you fight to focus your rage, grief, and sense of violation into something you can live with.
column2: 一名同僚開車送你回購物中心取車，你努力把滿腔的憤怒、悲傷與屈辱感，收攏成自己能承受的樣子。

column1: What you end up with is a burning desire to find and crucify the slime that hurt your wife.
column2: 最後剩下的，是一股想找出並嚴懲那個傷害你太太的人渣的熊熊怒火。

column1: Somebody out there picked the wrong man to mess with.
column2: 外頭有個傢伙，這次是惹錯人了。

column1: The chart shows that Marie's IV dosage is supposed to be set at 0.005
column2: 病歷表上顯示，Marie 的點滴劑量應該設定在 0.005。

column1: You gently kiss Marie's lips.
column2: 你輕輕吻了 Marie 的嘴唇。

column1: Sweet dreams!
column2: 祝妳好夢！

column1: You softly kiss your wife.  Her eyelids flicker in response.
column2: 你輕柔地吻了太太一下。她的眼皮微微顫動，像是有了回應。

column1: Doctor Wagner's face is grave as he says...
column2: Wagner 醫師神情凝重地說……

column1: I'm afraid I don't have any good news, Sonny.   Marie's condition is unchanged.
column2: 恐怕我沒有什麼好消息，Sonny。Marie 的狀況沒有改變。

column1: There's nothing more we can do but wait... and hope.
column2: 我們現在能做的，只剩下等待……和盼望。

column1: Again, I'm sorry, Officer.  Now if you'll excuse me, I have other patients to attend to.
column2: 再說一次，我很遺憾，警官。容我先失陪了，還有其他病人等著我。

column1: She seems to be resting quietly now.
column2: 她現在似乎正安靜地休息著。

column1: Hello, Sergeant Bonds.  I'm afraid there's no change.
column2: 你好，Bonds 警佐。恐怕還是沒有變化。

column1: Nothing new to report, I'm afraid.
column2: 恐怕沒有新的消息可以回報。

column1: We haven't noticed any changes, but I think she appreciates you being here, just the same.
column2: 我們沒有注意到什麼變化，不過我想她還是很感謝你在這裡陪著她。

column1: In an anxious voice, you tell the nurse you're concerned about the IV dosage.
column2: 你語帶焦急地向護理師表示，你對點滴的劑量感到擔心。

column1: I'll get the doctor to check on that right away, Officer.
column2: 我馬上請醫師來檢查一下，警官。

column1: Torn between feeling foolish and genuinely alarmed, you explain to the doctor that there seems to be a discrepancy between the IV dosage on the chart and that on the IV meter.
column2: 你一邊覺得自己是不是太多心，一邊又真的感到不安，向醫師解釋病歷表上的點滴劑量和點滴計上顯示的似乎對不上。

column1: The doctor looks doubtful as he checks the chart...
column2: 醫師一臉狐疑地翻看病歷表……

column1: ...Then the IV.
column2: ……接著又看了看點滴。

column1: With a red face, the doctor says...
column2: 醫師漲紅了臉說……

column1: Why...You're correct, Sergeant Bonds.   This dosage is obviously incorrect.
column2: 這……你說得沒錯，Bonds 警佐。這個劑量顯然不對。

column1: I don't understand this at all.  I can't believe our staff could make such a serious error!   I have readjusted the IV.  Perhaps Marie will feel better now.
column2: 我實在不明白怎麼會這樣。真不敢相信我們的人員會犯下這麼嚴重的錯誤！我已經重新調整了點滴，Marie 現在或許會好一些。

column1: Marie's eyelids flutter, almost as though she could hear her music box.
column2: Marie 的眼皮微微顫動，彷彿聽見了音樂盒的聲音。

column1: You could swear that you just saw Marie's finger move!
column2: 你敢發誓，你剛才看到 Marie 的手指動了一下！

column1: Marie's mouth moves slightly.
column2: Marie 的嘴唇微微動了一下。

column1: Marie's eyes finally open. The warmth of her smile gives you hope for the first time since her attack.   You're a lucky man, Sonny Bonds.  Marie is alive and whole.
column2: Marie 終於睜開了眼睛。她溫暖的笑容，是她遇襲以來你第一次感受到希望。你是個幸運的男人，Sonny Bonds。Marie 活著，而且完好無缺。

column1: Do you need something, Sergeant Bonds?
column2: 你有什麼需要嗎，Bonds 警佐？

column1: If there is nothing else, I have to get back to work.
column2: 如果沒別的事，我得回去工作了。

column1: I never lost hope!  I just knew that somehow, someway, you would come back to me.
column2: 我從沒放棄希望！我就是知道，不管用什麼方法，妳一定會回到我身邊。

column1: It was your strength and your will to live that brought you back.
column2: 是妳的堅強和求生意志，把妳帶回來的。

column1: You're going to be fine now sweetness. You'll be up and around in no time.
column2: 妳現在會沒事的，甜心。妳很快就能下床走動了。

column1: There's no doubt in my mind, somebody up there is looking out for you.
column2: 我很確定，上天在保佑著妳。

column1: We're real close to nailing the animals that caused this.
column2: 我們已經快抓到做這件事的畜生了。

column1: The digital readout indicates Marie's IV dosage.
column2: 數位顯示幕上顯示著 Marie 的點滴劑量。

column1: One moment, Sir.
column2: 請稍等，長官。

column1: That won't help Marie come back.  They're doing all they can.
column2: 那樣做對 Marie 醒來沒有幫助。他們已經盡力了。

column1: You've already introduced yourself to the hospital staff.
column2: 你已經向醫院的工作人員自我介紹過了。

column1: Marie is resting gently.  You don't want to disturb her.
column2: Marie 正安穩地休息著，你不想打擾她。

column1: You gently place a fresh rose in Marie's hand.   However, there is no response.  Nice try Sonny.
column2: 你輕輕把一朵新鮮玫瑰放進 Marie 手中，然而她毫無反應。這次沒成功，Sonny。

column1: Marie's condition might yet be reversible.  Don't give up without a fight.
column2: Marie 的狀況或許還有機會扭轉，別輕易放棄。

column1: You can't change the medication by yourself.
column2: 你不能自己更改藥物用量。

column1: The room temperature is monitored carefully by the staff.   You don't need to open the window.
column2: 病房的溫度有工作人員仔細控管，你不需要開窗。

column1: Marie lies awake in the bed.
column2: Marie 醒著躺在床上。

column1: Marie lies motionless on the hospital bed.
column2: Marie 一動也不動地躺在病床上。
